session_read: Pre-open, Wed 26 Aug. The tape is calm — Asia green across the board, VIX 15.69, SMH +1.65% on Tuesday's close — and the gate reads AMBIGUOUS only because neither future quite reached zero. That is a classification technicality, not a warning. The real story sits inside the book. The wallet has been drained a second time: $3,499 went out overnight across eight buys, and cash now stands at $124.52, or 0.30% of the book against a [5,15]% band. Every dollar is at work, which means the desk has no answer to a drawdown that does not begin with a sale. Aggregate open ATR risk is 13.03% against a 10% cap, with eight positions over their own caps — the deployment re-levered a book the August stops had de-levered, the same pattern as 19-20 August. Two new names arrived, LITE and SMCI, and both are now banded; classifying them lifted the AI-capex chain to 84.50% purely on bookkeeping, not repricing. This remains one bet wearing six labels. NVDA reports tonight. Notably, it did not run into the print.
